dominant_breach: a disability benefit can be legally claimable while still arriving too late to preserve housing, health, credit, work attachment, or household stability
fastest_washout: hearing delay, evidentiary burden, lost interim income, health deterioration, housing instability, and debt accumulation wash out the value of an eventual award

remedy_operability_gate.note: SSA performance and OHO wait-time sources turn disability appeal latency into a measurable relief-timing defect, not a generic bureaucracy complaint.

appeal_latency_and_time_to_relief.note: Hearing-processing and wait-time data must be scored against rent, health, credit, and household-stability timelines; eventual eligibility does not preserve the claimant if relief arrives too late.

interim_protection_before_irreversible_l.note: The key missing proof is whether claimants have bridge income, housing preservation, health access, and debt-protection rails during appeal latency.

benefit_payment_timeliness.note: SSA performance targets provide an official operational denominator, but the cube needs claimant-tail outcomes and payment restoration speed.

claimant_standing_access.note: Standing exists through the administrative appeal path, but ordinary claimants need navigation, representation, and evidence support to make it usable.

restoration_after_wrongful_denial.note: Backpay can repair some delayed cash, but it may not restore lost housing, credit, health continuity, or family support; restoration evidence is missing.

remedial_data_logging_and_auditability.note: Processing-time dashboards are a useful audit start, but they should be tied to claimant-incidence outcomes and interim harm.

proof_debt: median and tail appeal time by impairment, age, income, race, language, and representation
denial reversal rates and backpay restoration limits
local hearing-office variation and digital/offline access burdens

opening_package.hardening_lane: automatic interim supports and restoration beyond backpay

gate_11_enforceability_remedies.why: The remedy is not certified merely because an appeal exists; it must preserve the claimant while the appeal runs.

gate_02_floor_reality.why: Delayed disability relief can turn a nominal floor into an after-the-fact reimbursement.

gate_18_fresh_start_capacity.why: Backpay does not automatically repair credit, housing, medical, or household damage created during the benefit gap.

remedy_operability_register.claimant_perimeter: Applicants and appellants whose income/health stability depends on a disability claim
remedy_operability_register.standing_path: SSA reconsideration, hearing, Appeals Council, and court review sequence
remedy_operability_register.notice_explanation: Plain-language denial, missing-evidence, hearing, and status notices are needed for the path to be usable
remedy_operability_register.interim_protection: Uncertified; cube should require income, housing, medical, and credit-preservation rails while appeal remains pending
remedy_operability_register.time_to_relief: SSA publishes disability and hearing processing-time surfaces; time-to-relief must be scored directly
remedy_operability_register.review_body: Administrative law judge and appeals bodies, with court review later
remedy_operability_register.collective_or_representative_action: Representative and advocate access matters, but individual appeal remains the dominant path
remedy_operability_register.restoration_remedy: Backpay plus repair of collateral losses where delay caused housing, credit, health, or family-support damage
remedy_operability_register.enforcement_actor: SSA, representatives, administrative adjudicators, courts, congressional/inspector oversight
